paper_title: The Unseen Targets of Hate -- A Systematic Review of Hateful   Communication Datasets
caption: : Linguistic and geographic trends over time in harmful language research. Notably, the number of datasets for the non-top five languages continues to be lower than all English ones, while since 2017 we see more and more datasets in languages other than English.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the number of datasets in harmful language research across different languages from 2012 to 2022, with the vertical axis representing the number of datasets on a logarithmic scale (ranging from 10⁰ to 10²) and the horizontal axis showing the year. Each year is represented by a group of bars, with each bar corresponding to a specific language: English (blue), All other (orange), Arabic (green), Bengali (red), Spanish (purple), and Russian (brown), as indicated in the legend. The data shows that English consistently has the highest number of datasets throughout the period, often reaching values close to 100 (10²) in later years, particularly peaking in 2020 and 2021. The "All other" category (orange) also shows a steady increase, especially from 2017 onward, reaching approximately 10 datasets in 2022. Arabic, Spanish, and Russian datasets appear starting around 2017, with Arabic and Spanish showing moderate growth, reaching around 10 datasets by 2021, while Russian remains relatively low, with values around 1–2 in most years. Bengali datasets are sparse, appearing only from 2017 and remaining below 2 in all years. The bars are grouped by year and sorted chronologically, with no visual emphasis on any particular bar. The chart highlights a growing trend in non-English datasets, particularly from 2017, but English continues to dominate in quantity.
